evidence.paraphrase: Nārada goes to Kailāsa, asks Satī why she has not joined the festival where her sisters and their husbands rejoice, and says honor/dishonor is irrelevant in a father’s or husband’s home. Satī asks Śiva to accompany her. He warns that her father hates him and has not invited him, offering instead a local sacrifice if she creates sages/gods. She asks leave; he remains silent. She decides permission is unnecessary and leaves; amazed Śiva sends a vimāna accepting what will occur.

narrative_events.outcome: Śiva receives future reunion and present restoration of agency.

narrative_events.details: Restored to action and remembering Gaṇeśa, Śiva strikes his matted hair. Vīrabhadra arises with three heads, three feet and trident, bows as servant, receives the command to destroy Dakṣa and the sacrifice, laughs so the three worlds tremble, and creates innumerable Rudras from his body. Nandin-led Śiva Gaṇas follow.
narrative_events.outcome: Vīrabhadra and his generated Rudras march to the sacrifice.

narrative_events.details: Omens terrify sacrifice attendees. Vīrabhadra, Rudras, Nandin, Bhṛṅgiriṭi, Bhṛṅgin and Puṣpadanta attack; attendants flee, the pavilion is broken, gods/sages are beaten, wives are seized/beaten and taunted over husbands’ Śiva hostility, offerings eaten and altar defiled.
narrative_events.outcome: The sacrificial order is violently disrupted.

narrative_events.details: Śiva enters with bow/arrows and fights: he breaks Pūṣan’s teeth and removes Bhaga’s eyes. Nandin seizes Dharma, Bhṛṅgin Kaśyapa, Puṣpadanta beats Varuṇa, Bhairava seizes/fells Indra, Vīrabhadra fells Dakṣa. Viṣṇu fights and hurts Rudra/ghost forces; Śiva remembers Gaṇeśa and wounds Viṣṇu’s heart with arrows, felling him.
narrative_events.outcome: Viṣṇu is felled but then regains awareness.

narrative_events.details: Recovering, Viṣṇu releases the destructive Nārāyaṇa missile; Śiva releases Pāśupata. They fight in the sky and generate fire threatening earth and three worlds. Meanwhile Vīrabhadra treats Dakṣa as a sacrificial beast, cuts his head and offers it into fire. Viṣṇu hurls the cakra, which bows to Śiva and stops rather than striking him.
narrative_events.outcome: Dakṣa is beheaded; the cakra fails to attack Śiva.

narrative_events.details: Śiva raises his trident to kill Viṣṇu, but an unidentified heavenly voice forbids it and commands protection; Brahmā arrives, praises Śiva, warns against untimely destruction, and reconciles him with ashamed bowing Viṣṇu. Brahmā offers remaining oblations as Rudra’s share and asks restoration/restart. Śiva restores Bhaga’s eyes, makes Pūṣan a eater of ground food, and restores gods/sages/wives/servants to forms and radiance.
narrative_events.outcome: Viṣṇu survives and attendees are restored.

narrative_events.details: Because Dakṣa’s head was burnt, Śiva orders Bhṛṅgin to kill the first being he sees and bring its head. Bhṛṅgin sees a goat, kills it, brings its head; Śiva attaches it and revives Dakṣa. Brahmā prompts the now-humble Dakṣa to praise Śiva.
narrative_events.outcome: Dakṣa rises alive with a goat head.

narrative_events.details: Dakṣa’s hymn identifies Śiva with time-governed cosmic processes and asks pardon for pride. His goat-like speech delights Śiva, who restores his former human head, promises restored recognized Prajāpati chiefship, desired gifts and Śiva’s world to hymn-praisers, and fulfillment to one making the goat-like sound before him once. Śiva disappears, others return home, but Dakṣa remains distressed; the narrator explains temple bleating practice.
narrative_events.outcome: Human head and office restored; Dakṣa’s remaining distress leads to Mudgala teaching.
